2026-12-14.title: Third Monday of Annunciation · St John of the Cross
2026-12-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: A good tree bears good fruit
2026-12-14.alt: For St John of the Cross: 1 Corinthians 2:1–10; Luke 14:25–33.
2026-12-14.verse: The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good… for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
theo: Paul tells the Corinthians to “clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch… For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.” Sin tolerated in a community spreads like yeast; holiness requires decision.

Jesus teaches that each tree is known by its fruit, and words come from the heart's treasure. St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic, taught that the heart must be purified, even through dark nights, so that God alone may fill it. Before Christmas we ask: what is stored in my heart?
outline: Ask: what comes out of your mouth when you are tired or angry?
Point 1 · Clean out the old yeast
Sin must be removed, not tolerated.
Our deeds and words reveal our heart.
St John of the Cross: purification leads to union with God.
“Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.”
live: Watch your words today; replace one harsh word with a kind one.
Clean out the “old yeast” with a good confession.
saints: Carmelite friar, reformer with St Teresa of Ávila, mystic and Doctor of the Church, author of The Dark Night and The Living Flame of Love.
2026-12-14.prayer: Lord, purify my heart as you purified St John of the Cross, so that from its good treasure only good may come, and you alone may fill it. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana Christ our Passover is offered. We come to the altar with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, asking him to remove the old yeast of sin.

quick: Each tree is known by its fruit.
2026-12-14.action: Replace one harsh word with a kind one today.
2026-12-14.question: What treasure is stored in my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says a good tree gives good fruit. When our hearts are good, our words and actions are good too.
family.intention: We pray that our family may speak kind words at home.
family.ask: Ask: “What good ‘fruit’ did each of us give today?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, our Passover Lamb, cleanse us of the old yeast of sin. As we gather, make our hearts good trees that bear good fruit. Amen.
share: Paul says a little yeast leavens the whole batch (1 Corinthians 5:6). What small sin am I tolerating that could spread?
Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks (Luke 6:45). What do my words reveal about my heart?
What will I bring to confession before Christmas?
pm.resp: Create in us a clean heart, O God.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy and sincere in all her members.
For those trapped in sinful relationships and habits, that they may find the courage to change.
For Carmelites and all contemplatives, that through the prayers of St John of the Cross they may be filled with God.
For families, that their homes may be free of harsh words.
For all of us, that we may make a good confession this Nombu.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave St John of the Cross a love that grew even in darkness. Purify our hearts, make our words good fruit, and prepare us to celebrate your Son's birth with sincerity and truth. Amen.

illus: A farmer in Wayanad had a mango tree that gave sour, wormy fruit. Instead of cutting it down, he grafted a good branch onto the old trunk. In two years it bore sweet mangoes. Grace is God's graft on our old nature.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes very strongly to the Corinthians about a scandal in their community: a man living in an immoral relationship, and the community proud instead of grieving (1 Corinthians 5:1–2). Paul is not being harsh for its own sake. He knows that sin tolerated spreads.

He uses an image from the Passover: a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough. Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, for our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed; let us celebrate the festival with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth (1 Corinthians 5:6–8).

Before Passover, Jewish families searched the whole house for every crumb of yeast and threw it out. The Christmas fast is our search through the house of the heart: the old grudge, the hidden habit, the dishonest income, the bitter word. Confession is the cleaning.

In the Gospel Jesus says: no good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit; each tree is known by its own fruit; out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks (Luke 6:43–45). Our words reveal our hearts.

Today we remember St John of the Cross, the Carmelite mystic who taught that the soul must be emptied of attachments to be filled with God. He was imprisoned by his own brothers, yet wrote some of the most beautiful love poetry in the Church. A good tree, even in a dark cell, bore good fruit.

This week, let us listen to our own speech. What comes out of our mouth at home, at work, on social media? If it is criticism and complaint, the root needs care. Let us bring that root to confession before Christmas, and ask God for a heart from which good words flow. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit. When your heart is good, your words and actions will be good too!

intro: Theme: “Out of the abundance of the heart.”
A good tree, a clean heart; St John of the Cross.

sub: God promises to replace the heart of stone.
Conversion is God's work in us.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
No good tree bears bad fruit, nor again does a bad tree bear good fruit; for each tree is known by its own fruit.
points.apply: Ask God for a new heart in prayer today.

sub: Our words show what we store.
q: Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.
The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, and the evil person out of evil treasure produces evil; for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
points.apply: Replace one harsh word with a kind one today.

sub: The one who trusts God is like a tree by the stream.
St John of the Cross: God alone satisfies.
q: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: A good heart bears good fruit.
Let God purify and fill it.
2026-12-14.resolve: Examine your words each night this week.
